model_output.verdict: An Army logistics leader with a clear record of managing people, equipment, and vehicle readiness.
write_up: This is a strong transition resume! Your Army roles show the people, equipment, and maintenance work behind your move toward operations supervision. A recruiter can see both what you managed and what changed under your leadership.

The vehicle-readiness line is the standout: it gives the starting and ending rates and names the changes you made. Your progression from mechanic to platoon sergeant is easy to follow, and your in-progress supply chain degree supports the direction you've named.

Start by adding what you taught the junior mechanics, then move the readiness result higher in your latest role. Your resume itself is unlikely to be the main obstacle; the competitiveness of the jobs you target will also matter.

cards.cannot_tell: A recruiter can see how many mechanics you trained, but not what you taught them. The subject would show what expertise you passed on.
cards.question: What skills did you teach the junior mechanics?

cards.line: - Accountable for $14M of vehicles, tools, and equipment with zero losses on three annual inventories
cards.cannot_tell: Keep this as a model. It names the assets you were accountable for and gives the inventory record a recruiter can take away.

cards.line: - Led, trained, and evaluated 38 soldiers across maintenance, supply, and fuel sections
cards.cannot_tell: For a role one level above supervisor, the priorities and decisions behind your leadership would add another dimension.
cards.example: Led, trained, and evaluated 38 soldiers across maintenance, supply, and fuel sections, with responsibility for [team priorities] and [a decision you made]
cards.question: What priorities and decisions were yours across those sections?

cards.line: - Cut the unit's vehicle non-mission-capable rate from 18% to 6% in a year by changing the parts ordering process and the weekly maintenance schedule
cards.cannot_tell: Move this above the other Platoon Sergeant lines. It's your strongest example of changing a process and measuring the result.

fit.why: Your stated target and your leadership of maintenance, supply, and fuel sections point toward operations supervision.
fit.level: manager, led 38 soldiers and had 6 direct-report sergeants
fit.note: Your maintenance and logistics background also gives you a strong basis for supply chain supervision. When tailoring your resume, explain Army terms in language the employer uses without changing what you did.
